title: Canonical PCM And Drop-Anchor Refinement

decisionGates.description: After canonical PCM cache implementation, verify that analysis, debug waveform, nudge, and render all reference the same timing source.
After feature extraction and candidate export, inspect reports to confirm candidate features are interpretable and useful.
After generating drop-switch auditions from refined anchors, stop for user listening verdict before changing defaults.

subagentExecutionRules: Read this kiro.json, requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md, and all required steering context before executing tasks.
Use Rekordbox XML labels only as semantic truth/evaluation labels in this spec; do not leak them into automatic anchor selection except where a command explicitly benchmarks against truth.
Do not train a production ML model on only the current 48 songs. The 48-track set is for regression, feature inspection, and audition, not final training.
Do not replace the current working nudge path until the refined anchor path has generated audition artifacts and the user has accepted the result.
Do not independently snap every beat in the beatgrid. Any beatgrid refinement must preserve global phase and tempo continuity.
Use canonical PCM for every timing-sensitive path. Do not mix decoder outputs for analysis, waveform, nudge, and render.
Any transform that changes timing must emit sample-rate, frame-centering, hop-length, and source-timeline provenance.
Write generated PCM, feature stores, datasets, audition WAVs, and debug artifacts only under ignored local paths.
Stop at manual decision gates and record the user's verdict before marking those tasks complete.
